chapter_name: Poems by Milton (On His Blindness & On His Deceased Wife) by John Milton
learning_objective: 🎯 Understand John Milton's deeply personal struggles with blindness and grief, and see how faith helps him overcome despair!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: ग्रीक पौराणिक पात्र जिसने अपने पति के लिए जान दी

main_concepts.concept_title: 📜 On His Blindness (When I Consider How My Light is Spent)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Milton went blind in mid-life. He laments that his 'one talent' (writing poetry) is now useless and worries God will punish him for not serving Him actively.
Personified 'Patience' answers Milton's doubt: God does not need human work or gifts. 'They also serve who only stand and wait'—true devotion means accepting God's will patiently.

main_concepts.concept_title: 👁️ On His Deceased Wife (Methought I Saw My Late Espoused Saint)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A heartbreaking dream-vision sonnet about his late wife (likely Katherine Woodcock). Because he was blind when they married, he never saw her face in real life.
Milton compares his wife's return from death in his dream to Alcestis being rescued from the grave in Greek mythology, draped in pure white symbolizing innocence and heaven.

fun_activity.title: ⏳ The 14-Line Challenge
fun_activity.instructions: A Petrarchan sonnet has 14 lines divided into an octave (8 lines asking a question/problem) and a sestet (6 lines giving an answer/resolution). Try writing a short 4-line rhyme about overcoming a personal obstacle!

exam_tips: 📌 Quote the famous concluding line: 'They also serve who only stand and wait' and explain its meaning regarding humble submission to fate.
📌 Note the heartbreaking ending of 'On His Deceased Wife': just as she leans in to embrace him, he wakes up and 'day brought back my night' (his physical blindness returns).
📌 Understand the Biblical parable of the talents (Matthew 25) which Milton refers to in his blindness poem.
quick_recap: ⭐ Both poems are Petrarchan (Italian) sonnets expressing deeply autobiographical themes.
⭐ Milton feared his blindness would prevent him from writing his great epic poetry for God's glory.
⭐ In his dream, his deceased wife appears cleansed, radiant, and free from earthly imperfection.
